source.publication: Rhode Island Retirement Income Tax Guide, Publication 2026-01 (tax year 2025)
source.section: Instructions PDF pp.9-10, Schedule M line 1t, questions 1 and 2 and table lines 1-4; Guide PDF p.5 (annuities qualify); PDF pp.21-22, Section 5 Example #6 (married filing separately limit 107,000); Instructions PDF p.4, RI-1040 lines 1-5; PDF p.5, lines 6-8; PDF p.13, Tax Computation Worksheet ('Use for all filing status types')

worked: Federal AGI = annuity (person 0) 40,000.00 + interest 30,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction - 1 x 1,600.00 age 65+ = 52,650.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). RI-1040 line 1 federal AGI 70,000.00. Line 1t: question 1 born on or before March 1, 1959: person 0 born 1955-06-15 (age 70): yes; question 2 federal AGI 70,000.00 less than or equal to 107,000.00: yes. Table: person 0 line 2 40,000.00, line 3 lesser of that and 50,000.00 = 40,000.00; line 4 = 40,000.00. Line 1y total decreasing modifications = 40,000.00. Line 2a other-state obligations 0.00; line 2m total increasing modifications = 0.00. Schedule M page 2 line 3 net = 0.00 - 40,000.00 = -40,000.00; RI-1040 line 2 = -40,000.00. Line 3 modified federal AGI = 70,000.00 + (-40,000.00) = 30,000.00. Standard Deduction and Exemption Worksheets: line 3 30,000.00 is not more than 254,250.00: the worksheets stop at line 3, full amounts. Line 4 standard deduction: 10,900.00 (Married filing separately). Line 5 = 30,000.00 - 10,900.00 = 19,100.00. Line 6 exemptions: 1 x 5,100.00 = 5,100.00. Line 7 taxable income = 19,100.00 - 5,100.00 = 14,000.00. Line 8 tax on 14,000.00 by the schedule as numbers: 14,000.00 x 0.0375 = 525.000000 = 525.00. Credits 0.00 (Schedule I, Schedule II, RI earned income credit and RI-1040H are not modelled and not claimed here). Rhode Island income tax = 525.00. Note: An annuity on federal line 5b, on a separate return.
